newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Explorers Index rises in week.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Explorers Index rises in week.

text.p: Stockbroker Eyres Reed Ltd said its Australian Explorers Index rose nine points or 0.32 percent last week. The All Ordinaries index fell 1.39 percent.
Sept 6 Aug 30 pct 1 Month 1 Year pct
NOTE: The explorers index (base 500, March 1992) tracks the performance of 88 small capitalisation exploration companies.
The Eyres Reed Explorer Index rose nine points this week in a very reactive punting market, Eyres Reed analyst Glen Colgan said in a commentary.
"The underlying selling tone of the general market was offset by a thirst for 20 percent plus turns in the specs," Colgan said.
Falls outnumbered rises five to four. "The success of the (Joe) Gutnick stable in recent weeks served as a catalyst for the 'defiance of fundamentals' attitude," he said.
The stars of the week were Paget Mining and Strategic Minerals.
Paget Mining Co Ltd, up to 53 cents from 29 cents in two days, is fighting to retain title to the Sabodala gold project Senegal, West Africa.
Strategic Minerals Corp NL, which ran to 11.5 cents from 6.5 cents, reported a narrow, high grade drill intercept from the Woolgar gold prospect in Queensland.

Others on the gallop included Federation Resources ML, up to 12.5 cents from 8.4 cents, Mt Grace Gold Mining NL (up to six cents from 4.5), Plenty River Mining Co Ltd (up to 3.9 cents from 3.o), Comet Gold NL (up to 18 cents from 14) and GME Resources (up to 12 cents from 9.5).

The softness elsewhere was reflected by falls in Gallery Resources NL (which fell to 25 cents from 35), Tectonic Resources Ltd (down to 10 cents from 12.5), Platsearch (down to six cents from 7.8), East Coast Minerals NL (dwon to 20 cents from 25) and the further descent of the Amity Oil share price (down to 52 cents from 64 cents).
